# Jubilees Chapter 19 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 19:3 — "We tested him" — angelic surveillance of Abraham's grief

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "we tried him [to see] whether his spirit was patient" | "Tried" with bracketed gloss |
| LOGOS | "We tested him to see whether his spirit was patient" | "Tested" |
| PNEUMA | "The angels watched to see whether he would keep his peace" | "Watched" — shifts from testing to observing |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Tested" accurately renders the Ge'ez active verb (the angels administer a test). PNEUMA's "watched" makes them passive observers, which misrepresents their role. EMET's bracket is unnecessary.

---

## 19:4 — "double cave" vs. "cave of Machpelah"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the land of the double cave" | Literal Ge'ez — "double cave" |
| LOGOS | "the land of the cave of Machpelah" | Uses the established Hebrew toponym |
| PNEUMA | "the cave of Machpelah" | Same as LOGOS |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Cave of Machpelah" is the established toponym; "double cave" (EMET) is a Ge'ez rendering that translates rather than transliterates the place name. The toponym should be preserved.

---

## 19:14 — "they came to be called Arabs and Ishmaelites"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "their name was called Arabs, and Ishmaelites" | Passive naming |
| LOGOS | "came to be called Arabs and Ishmaelites" | Idiomatic English |
| PNEUMA | "became one people, known as Arabs and Ishmaelites" | "One people" added |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The Ge'ez says they "were called" by these names; "came to be called" is natural English. PNEUMA's "one people" adds unification not stated in the source — the text describes mingling, not political unification.

---

## 19:25 — "no accepting of persons" vs. "no partiality"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "no accepting of persons and no receiving of gifts" | Literal Ge'ez idiom |
| LOGOS | "no partiality and no taking of gifts" | "Partiality" for "accepting of persons" |
| PNEUMA | "doesn't play favorites, he doesn't take bribes" | Colloquial rendering |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "Partiality" is the established English rendering of "accepting/lifting of faces" (the Semitic idiom). "Play favorites" (PNEUMA) is accurate but too casual for Abraham's formal testament. "Taking of gifts" (LOGOS) vs. EMET's "receiving of gifts" — minor; LOGOS preferred.

---

## 19:29 — "blessing of the first-born" — transfer to Jacob

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "he gave him the blessing of the first-born, and spoke to him regarding what befits the first-born" | Full literal double reference |
| LOGOS | "He gave Jacob the blessing of the firstborn and spoke with him about what befits the firstborn" | Same with "Jacob" named |
| PNEUMA | "He gave Jacob the blessing reserved for the firstborn and explained what it meant to carry that responsibility" | "Explained what it meant to carry that responsibility" paraphrases |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. "What befits the firstborn" is the Ge'ez formula for the rights and duties of primogeniture. PNEUMA's "carry that responsibility" is interpretive.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
